To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel unsupervised one-to-many translation method for image translation that is completely unsupervised, and that we show that our method can be used for a variety of tasks such as domain translation, image generation, image editing, etc.

(1) we propose a novel unsupervised image translation model that is able to learn a mapping between a source and a target domain while preserving relevant underlying shared semantics; (2) we show that our model is able to perform one-to-many image translations between a source and target domains while learning a mapping that preserves relevant underlying shared semantics
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following research questions:

    \item How can we perform unsupervised image to image translation in a completely unsupervised setting, without any supervision or labels?
the following question: \textit{How can we learn to translate images between different domains, without requiring any paired training data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a method for learning an unsupervised one-to-many mapping between image domains.

we present a novel unsupervised one-to-many image-to-image translation framework that learns to translate an input image to a distribution of plausible outputs, while maintaining the underlying semantics of the image, and we show that the proposed approach outperforms the state of the art on a wide range of unsupervised one to many image translation tasks

our model learns a mapping $f: \mathbf{x} \mapsto \mathbf{y}$ such that $\mathbf{x} = f(\mathbf{y})$ and $\mathbf{y} = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}})$, where $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{\hat{x}}$ are images from domain $X$ while $\mathbf{Y}$ is an image from domain $Y$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose an unsupervised image-to-image translation framework which learns a shared latent representation between two domains, and then uses the learned representation to translate an image between two domains.
we propose a method that can translate an image from $X$ into a distribution of plausible images from $Y$.
we are able to learn a mapping from a source domain to a target domain without any paired training data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn a shared representation between two domains that is useful for image translation, without requiring any supervision in the form of aligned image pairs.
the use of a single domain-specific encoder is enough to perform unsupervised one-to-many image to image translation, and that the use of an auxiliary encoder is not needed.
the use of adversarial loss alone is sufficient to learn such one-to-many translation.
